en: and so on.
zh: 等等。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: If you spend time on the negatives, you're not gonna get that like same thing.
zh: 如果你把时间花在消极面上，你不会得到同样的结果。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So that becomes later when you have a more adoption already, then you're like, okay, why are you still resisting?
zh: 所以这就变成后来当你已经有了更多的采用，然后你会说，好吧，你为什么还在抗拒？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: We've offered you all the information, we've seen scale like parts of it in the org.
zh: 我们已经向你提供了所有的信息，我们已经看到了组织内部的部分规模化。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: What is holding you back?
zh: 是什么在阻碍你？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And that could be a variety of reasons in there.
zh: 那可能有各种各样的原因。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Now, it probably makes sense is not to over-rotate on one team going all the way and nobody else.
zh: 现在，合理的做法可能不是过度依赖一个团队走到最后，而其他人却无动于衷。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So I would say there's like a leveling up, they spearhead the thing, and then you bring others maybe on kind of like parts of the journey already, and then they kind of like drive kind of towards what the one team is doing.
zh: 所以我会说，这有一个升级的过程，他们带头做这件事，然后你把其他人带上来，也许是在旅程的某些部分已经进行中，然后他们有点像是在朝着那个团队在做的事情前进。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So is it a fair assessment to say you want to make the fast teams go as fast as they possibly can and allow then, and then the the enablement is more for the teams that are following to say, let's share the and let's share and educate them based on the best practices that these fast teams are going.
zh: 所以这样说是否公平：你想让快速团队尽可能快地前进，然后允许，然后赋能更多的是针对跟随的团队，让我们分享，并基于这些快速团队正在进行的最佳实践来分享和教育他们。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And how can we enable you to take practices that work for your teams that you know learning from these from these almost like leading teams?
zh: 我们如何赋能你采用对你团队有效的实践，你知道，这是从这些几乎像领先的团队那里学到的？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: But it's a typical transformation play.
zh: 但这是一种典型的转型策略。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: I have a hackathon, I share stuff, I have a lunch and learn, I share the success stories, I celebrate like whatever team is doing the best thing.
zh: 我举办一个黑客马拉松，我分享东西，我举办一个午餐学习会，我分享成功故事，我表扬无论哪个团队正在做最好的事情。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So that that that's kind of very common in kind of driving adoption.
zh: 所以这是在推动采用中非常普遍的做法。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: This is DevOps, this is cloud, this is developer security, it's all the same styles.
zh: 这是 DevOps，这是云，这是开发者安全，都是同样的风格。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Correct.
zh: 正确。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Now we're given all the success stories, what and that's the reason why I talk about the organizational enablement.
zh: 现在我们已经给出了所有的成功故事，这就是为什么我谈论组织赋能的原因。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: A lot of what happened in the organizations is that well, we'll give everybody the tools, yeah.
zh: 组织中发生的大部分情况是，我们会给所有人提供工具，是的。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And some will pick it up and they go all the way and kind of they build their own future and and they become very proactive.
zh: 有些人会接受它并一直做下去，他们会构建自己的未来，并且变得非常主动。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Um initially, everybody was measuring adoption by saying, well, is everybody using a tool?
zh: 最初，每个人都通过说“好吧，大家都在使用这个工具吗？”来衡量采用情况。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Okay, so that's one way of saying, like, okay, there we have some kind of uh scaling within the org.
zh: 好吧，这是一种表达方式，比如，好的，我们在组织内有某种程度的规模化。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Then people said, Well, we're gonna look at like the people who go crazy on the tokens, that's usage, right?
zh: 然后人们说，好吧，我们要看看那些在 tokens 上疯狂使用的人，那就是使用情况，对吧？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: It's a substitute proxy kind of measurement where you say, Well, you know, the people are using more tokens, they're like at least enthusiastic about it, but they might not be using this quite efficiently.
zh: 这是一种替代性的代理指标，你会说，好吧，你知道，人们在使用更多的 tokens，他们至少对此很有热情，但他们可能并没有非常高效地使用它。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: If I were to put one measurement right now is how much these people are contributing to the shared components and they're fixing the system instead of kind of using more or having a tool.
zh: 如果我现在要提出一个衡量指标，那就是这些人有多少在为共享组件做贡献，以及他们在修复系统，而不是仅仅使用更多或者拥有一个工具。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Because if you that gives the more uh buildup of like people improving the shared context, because one context improvement impacts other teams, and that is a typically another skill from like I can be personally very effective to this is the skill that like helps the whole org, and that's a different measurement.
zh: 因为如果你这样做，就能更多地建立人们改进共享上下文的积累，因为一次上下文的改进会影响其他团队，这通常是一种不同于我个人可以非常高效的技能，这是一种帮助整个组织的技能，这是一种不同的衡量指标。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And the measurement there is how many touches does the human still need to do for an agent to do the right thing, and so kind of measuring that becomes more effective than measuring uh you know, kind of adoption just by having license counts.
zh: 那里的衡量指标是，为了让智能体做正确的事情，人类仍然需要进行多少次触碰，所以衡量那个比仅仅通过许可数量来衡量采用更有效。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Uh, and if you put that into practice, you'll see like like sharing uh across actually helps that metric to because if you fix it for one, your numbers go up in all the teams.
zh: 而且，如果你将其付诸实践，你会看到，实际上分享有助于那个指标，因为如果你为一个团队修复了它，你在所有团队的数字都会上升。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: But it's uh it's I guess that's a driving towards that like more almost like autonomous factory that we're building.
zh: 但这，我想这是在驱动我们正在建立的更像自主工厂的东西。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: But I think that is the new metric.
zh: 但我认为这就是新的衡量指标。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Uh, who the people who uh contribute to that metric are the ones that are really helping you on the journey.
zh: 那些为该指标做出贡献的人，才是真正在旅程中帮助你的人。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Uh not uh the the token billionaires.
zh: 而不是那些 token 亿万富翁。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Yeah, yeah, no.
zh: 是的，是的，不。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So a lot of the conversations that we've had here, it kind of like reminds me of um some of the work that we're doing on Tesla Agent, which is which is you know really maps nicely to some of the ways that we that you're talking about the growth and the scaling.
zh: 所以我们在这里进行的很多对话，让我想起了我们在 Tesla Agent 上做的一些工作，这，你知道，非常好地映射到了你谈论增长和规模化的一些方式。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um, first of all, if we go back to when you were talking about creating context, sharing that context uh and making that context the best it can be.
zh: 首先，如果我们回到当你谈论创建上下文、分享那个上下文并使那个上下文尽可能好的时候。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: I love the way that you kind of mentioned for people who are who don't want to move to agentic because they feel like you know it's not good enough, it's not where it is.
zh: 我很喜欢你提到的那种方式，对于那些不想转向智能体的人，因为他们觉得，你知道，这还不够好，还没达到那个水平。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: I love the fact that you say make them do a lot of work on the skills because that's how you actually get the most out of it.
zh: 我喜欢你说让他们在技能上做大量工作的这一点，因为这就是你如何真正从中获得最大收益的方式。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Now, Tesla Agent, of course, uh is is an agent that allows you to uh to really make those changes well, not just um you know you allowing the agent to make those changes with your guidance, but also based on facts from logs and pull requests that have been uh historically done in those projects.
zh: 现在，Tesla Agent，当然，是一个允许你真正做出这些改变的智能体，不仅仅是，你知道你允许智能体在你的指导下做出这些改变，而且是基于这些项目中历史上完成的日志和 pull requests 的事实。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um so that that feels like a really strong way to kind of like map Tesla Agent to some of those things, but also the way that Tesla Agent doesn't try and provide you with a software factory out of the box.
zh: 所以这感觉是一种非常强有力的方式，可以将 Tesla Agent 映射到其中一些事情，还有 Tesla Agent 并不试图为你提供一个开箱即用的软件工厂的方式。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: What it does is it provides you with a path so that over time you'll get closer and closer and closer to a software factory.
zh: 它所做的是为你提供一条路径，这样随着时间的推移，你会越来越接近一个软件工厂。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: So a big piece of this growing step by step and and and you know, optimizing as much as we can do uh in our context and our skills and things like that, as valuable as that is, we need some level of automation to make sure that this is being done continuously.
zh: 所以这种一步一步增长的一部分，以及，你知道，在我们的上下文、技能等方面尽可能优化，尽管这很有价值，但我们需要一定程度的自动化来确保这一点是持续完成的。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Um so so how can we, you know, what what's a good process of being able to build that that automation of the optimization into our in into our daily work?
zh: 那么，所以我们怎样才能，你知道，什么是好的流程，能够将这种优化自动化构建到我们的日常工作中？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Um maybe I'll first say kind of the parallel with DevOps, right?
zh: 也许我首先说一点与 DevOps 的类比，对吧？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: A lot of it initially was like, oh, can we deploy faster?
zh: 很大一部分最初像是，噢，我们能更快地部署吗？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Can we kind of make sure it's happening?
zh: 我们能确保它正在发生吗？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: But then the whole monitoring became observability, and ultimately that was the feedback channel of the automation.
zh: 但是后来整个监控变成了可观测性，最终那是自动化的反馈渠道。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Like, what do we need to improve?
zh: 像，我们需要改进什么？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Right.
zh: 对的。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So, and and I think part of what you see with the agents, whether that's your your skills optimizer that you can put in the loop that it makes you better, uh, whether that's your harness tool that detects uh things you're doing over and over again that could benefit maybe from better context or becoming a script or a deterministic thing.
zh: 所以，我认为你在智能体上看到的部分内容，无论是你在循环中放入的让你变得更好的技能优化器，还是你检测到的那些反复做的事情、可能受益于更好的上下文或成为脚本或确定性事物的 harness 工具。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So kind of those feedback loops uh will help you scale this out because you can only do so much in like you contributing the system, but if it's almost like a positive feedback loop that improves this over time and gives you hints uh like what to improve, I I think that's really powerful.
zh: 所以这些反馈循环将帮助你规模化扩展，因为你只能为系统做这么多贡献，但如果它几乎像一个积极的反馈循环随着时间的推移改进它并给你提示，比如需要改进什么，我认为那非常强大。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Now, the danger of a loop is that it could be a positive enemy.
zh: 现在，循环的危险在于它可能是一个积极的敌人。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So, you know, once a rule is accepted, it could go wrong, but that's why you need testing, the regression testing, uh, also for harnesses, for anything you put in there, that it's not just I edit and I pray whether it works.
zh: 所以，你知道，一旦一个规则被接受，它可能会出错，但这就是为什么你需要测试，回归测试，还有针对 harnesses，针对你放在那里的任何东西，它不仅仅是我编辑并祈祷它能工作。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Uh, but it's it's crucial because I I I often say if you have continuous delivery and everything's automated, and now with AI, you know, another part is being automated, the continuous learning is where the knowledge compounds.
zh: 但是这至关重要，因为我经常说如果你有持续交付并且一切都是自动化的，现在有了 AI，你知道，另一部分正在被自动化，持续学习就是知识复利的地方。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And and that seems to be becoming the moat of a company.
zh: 而且这似乎正在成为一家公司的护城河。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Like, how fast can you learn?
zh: 比如，你的学习速度能有多快？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: How fast can you adapt to a new ID?
zh: 你适应新 ID 的速度能有多快？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: How fast can you do it?
zh: 你能做到多快？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Like, even if that means rewriting the whole code base, it doesn't matter.
zh: 比如，即使这意味着重写整个代码库，也没关系。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: But like, how fast can you get that?
zh: 但是，你能多快做到这一点？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And and you can't do this with without a feedback loop uh helping you to improve that.
zh: 而且如果没有反馈循环帮助你改进，你无法做到这一点。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And this is a great target, essentially, to make sure we can become as effective as we can be, but it all comes at a cost as well, right?
zh: 这是一个很好的目标，本质上是确保我们要尽可能高效，但这也有代价，对吧？

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And and and there's a section here, obviously, in on scaling the org, which is cost management.
zh: 显然，这里有一部分是关于扩展组织的，也就是成本管理。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Now, last year people were just kind of like very much free to let's try and experiment as much as we can, let's try and get as much usage as we can to understand what works, what doesn't.
zh: 去年，人们有点像非常自由，让我们尽可能多地尝试和实验，让我们尽可能多地使用，以了解什么有效，什么无效。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: This year, budgets are a little bit more constrained, and people are thinking more about the return on the investment and how you manage the cost of everything that you're doing.
zh: 今年，预算有点更紧张了，人们更多地考虑投资回报率以及如何管理你所做的一切的成本。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Tell us a little bit about um how important I guess the optimizations are and this automation to make sure we're reeling in a little bit of that cost and we are getting a return rather than just you know those billionaire token users that we hear of.
zh: 请告诉我们一点关于优化和这种自动化有多重要，以确保我们能够稍微收回一些成本，并获得回报，而不仅仅是我们要听到的那些那些亿万富翁代币用户。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: I've been in the position as a VP where I had to say, like, oh, look at my budget, and the first year that AI came out, there was no budget for AI, so where am I looking for it?
zh: 我曾担任过 VP 的职位，我不得不像这样说，哦，看看我的预算，在 AI 出现的第一年，没有 AI 的预算，所以我该去哪里找呢？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Um, so I know it's a struggle, and especially with like a lot of the vendors raising their pricing models or changing their pricing models that we didn't cater for.
zh: 所以我知道这是一种挣扎，特别是随着许多供应商提高他们的定价模式或改变我们没有计入在内的定价模式。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Now you can have the instant reaction, say, Oh, well, everybody stop doing, let's remove, kind of like the like reduce the budget and uh kind of make sure that like we we we keep within limits.
zh: 现在你可以有即时的反应，说，哦，好吧，大家都停止做，让我们移除，有点像减少预算，并确保我们要保持在限度内。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: The problem then is you won't be going on that journey of learning because if you're limiting people, they they kind of like work wrong, oh I'll still do it manually because I don't have enough tokens and kind of go from there.
zh: 然后的问题是你将无法继续那段学习之旅，因为如果你限制了人们，他们就会有点像工作方式不对，哦，我还是要手动做，因为我没有足够的代币，然后就这样做。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Now, others people have kind of start assigning maybe more use cases.
zh: 现在，其他人已经开始分配更多的用例了。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So instead of it saying it the agent got better now, is it actually useful for that?
zh: 所以与其说智能体现在变好了，它实际上对那件事有用吗？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So I think the way you have to look at air or and and cost management is you know, I need to have a budget for people learning, and I need to have a budget that's useful, but the constraint of a budget should actually drive you in optimizing that loop because a lot of the people are blindly spending tokens, they're using Biggest model out of things, they are doing the same thing over and over where there could have been a context change or a harness change that would save them a lot of tokens.
zh: 所以我认为你看 AI 或成本管理的方式是，你知道，我需要有人们学习的预算，我需要有有用的预算，但预算的约束实际上应该驱动你去优化那个循环，因为很多人在盲目地花费代币，他们使用最大的模型，他们一遍又一遍地做同样的事情，而实际上可以通过上下文更改或某种利用方式的更改来为他们节省很多代币。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So if your organization is not your mature, you feel like you're over, you know, using things.
zh: 所以如果你的组织不成熟，你觉得你过度了，你知道，过度使用了东西。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And um, the parallel in the cloud was like when everybody went to the cloud, every system was a VM.
zh: 而且，云中的平行案例就像当每个人都去云上时，每个系统都是一个 VM。

speaker: SPEAKER_02
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And everyone's like, this is proving more costly.
zh: 每个人都说，这证明成本更高。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And then we learn techniques to put it like on the same instance and kind of like work from there.
zh: 然后我们学习技术把它放在同一个实例上，并像那样工作。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So I think we're in that phase, but it's it's very risky now for maybe a VP to say, let's close down the full budget and kind of stop the usage, because then your organization doesn't have that.
zh: 所以我认为我们处于那个阶段，但现在对于 VP 来说说，让我们关闭全部预算并停止使用是非常有风险的，因为那样你的组织就没有那个了。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: I think the the right reaction is where are we open spending?
zh: 我认为正确的反应是我们在哪里盲目地花费？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: But you need to have like observability for your FinOps, for your coding agents, and so on.
zh: 但你需要对你的 FinOps、对你的编码智能体等具有可观测性。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: So you need to work on the telemetry and then say, well, there's no habits, don't use this for that.
zh: 所以你需要研究遥测数据，然后说，好吧，这里没有习惯，不要把这个用于那个。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And kind of have a team work on the optimization instead of just closing the budget off.
zh: 并让一个团队负责优化，而不仅仅是关闭预算。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And let's say, you know, as a VP of engineering, uh, would you say, actually, of all my of all my children, all my teams, I do have preferences over where I want to spend money.
zh: 比如说，你知道，作为工程副总裁，你会说，实际上，在我所有的所有孩子中，我所有的团队中，我确实对我想在哪里花钱有偏好。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And actually the teams that are the highest performing, the ones that are experimenting, I almost want to give them free reign.
zh: 实际上，对于那些表现最高的、正在进行实验的团队，我几乎想给他们自由支配权。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Whereas the others, I do want to make sure they're that they're not just you know being ridiculous with their spend because we're not actually learning things as much from them.
zh: 而对于其他团队，我确实想确保他们没有你知道，在他们的开支上很荒谬，因为我们实际上并没有从他们那里学到多少东西。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: We're just trying to it is about ROI, it's about can we do things better in a cost-effective way?
zh: 我们只是试图它是关于 ROI，它是关于我们能否以具有成本效益的方式做得更好？

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Whereas these other teams are actually, even if they're spending money and not doing that, we're learning, okay, that's not a path to go, but it's money well spent.
zh: 而这些其他团队实际上是，即使他们花钱并没有做到那一点，我们也在学习，好吧，那不是一条可行之路，但这是钱花得值。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: And I think that's the struggle you have with the CFO who says, like, oh, where's the ROI, where's the ROI?
zh: 我认为这就是你和 CFO 面临的挣扎，CFO 会说，哦，ROI 在哪里，ROI 在哪里？

speaker: Patrick Debois
en: Like they're willing to spend if there's a return.
zh: 就像如果有回报，他们愿意花钱。
